nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵1/6
While China's HMPV outbreak grabs global headlines, similar or more severe virus outbreaks in the US and Europe are underreported. @WHO confirms China's cases follow seasonal trends, yet alarmist media coverage persists. 
My latest for @trtworld 👇🏽
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c https://t.co/8UrZxa2rzD

nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵2/6
"Some sensationalistic Western and Indian media are hyping Chinese cases... Yet leading platforms seem more balanced," @mahoneyshanghai of @ECNUER tells me. Meanwhile, the US faces flu & Norovirus surges; Europe battles RSV & Mpox. 
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c

nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵3/6
HMPV, first identified in 2001, isn’t new. It causes cold-like symptoms, mainly in children & the elderly. @WHO: China’s respiratory infections follow seasonal trends, with no unusual patterns or overwhelmed healthcare.
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c

nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵4/6
Post-COVID, media often treats infections as crises. “There’s just this tendency post-COVID to treat every infectious-disease event as an emergency, even when it’s not,” @AmeshAA tells @washingtonpost.
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c

nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵5/6 
HMPV coverage shows how post-COVID fears distort disease threats, especially with images from China. "Western media rarely hesitates to portray China in the worst light," says @mahoneyshanghai, citing bias and clickbait that public perception.
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c

nodes.author: abhishekbhaya
nodes.text:
🧵6/6
Ironically, outbreaks in China often come to global attention through official announcements by Chinese authorities, only to be misused by media for alarmist narratives. If such bias persists, could it discourage 🇨🇳from openly announcing outbreaks?
https://t.co/JavqrijA2c
